_comment: Mockup Reveal Scripts v2 — for prospects we already built a free working homepage mockup for. v2: reframed 'free' (the PREVIEW is free to look at, not a permanent free asset — the finished, hosted, live build is still the paid product), added light qualifying so real intel gets captured instead of just a yes/no on a link, and a real closing progression instead of a passive 'call me back.'

greeting.no_contact_default: Hey — is the owner around? Quick call about {business_name}.

word_for_word.label: Word for Word
word_for_word.script: Hey {first_name} — {rep_name} calling, Urban Niche Co. Straight up, this is a cold call — but I did more than homework. I actually built {business_name} a working homepage. It's live right now, you can see it today. Costs you nothing to look. Want the link?

guided.label: Guided
anchors: Say it's a cold call — upfront, always
"I built {business_name} a working homepage, it's live right now" — proof, not a promise
Ask permission to send the link. That's the whole ask — don't oversell the free part.

freestyle.label: Freestyle
freestyle.goal: Get them to look at the mockup. That's the entire call.
reminders: Lead with the cold call declaration
The mockup is the hook — you already did the work, that's rare and it lands
Ask for the best way to send it (text or email), then stop talking

opener.training_note: This is the strongest opener in the playbook — you're not selling an idea, you're handing over a finished thing. Say 'I built' not 'I designed a concept.' Don't say 'free' more than once and never say 'no catch' — it undersells what comes next. The preview is free to look at. Getting it finished, hosted on their own domain, and actually live is the paid part — that's where the real conversation goes once they're hooked.

qualify._note: Two or three questions, max — only after they've agreed to look. This isn't a full discovery call, it's intel-gathering disguised as normal conversation. Use the capture chips in the notes panel to log answers fast.

prompts.q: Real quick — is anybody handling your marketing right now, or has it mostly been word of mouth?
And I'm guessing you're the one who'd make the call on something like this?
If I got this fully finished — live on your own domain, actually working — is that something you'd want, or were you just curious to see it?

qualify.training_note: Ask these AFTER they engage, not before — you already earned the conversation with the build. Q1 tells you if there's a current vendor to work around. Q2 confirms you're not pitching a non-decision-maker. Q3 is the real one — their answer decides whether this becomes a close-now call or a nurture.

YES_SEND_IT.label: Yes — send it over
YES_SEND_IT.script: Perfect. Best number to text it to, or you want it by email? {mockup_url} — and while I've got you, quick one: is that something you'd actually want live and finished if I built it out for real, or were you just curious to see it?
YES_SEND_IT.training_note: Confirm the send method out loud first, then ask the real-interest question immediately — you have their attention right now, don't wait for a callback that might not come. Their answer decides whether you push toward WANTS_BUILD/HOT or log MOCKUP_SENT and nurture.

WHY_FREE.label: Why would you do this for free?
WHY_FREE.script: Because showing beats telling — I'd rather you see it than take my word for it. This part's free. If you want it finished — hosted on your own domain, actually live and working — that's the part that costs something, same as any of my other clients. But looking costs you nothing.
WHY_FREE.training_note: Say the quiet part out loud before they wonder about it — 'this part's free, the finished version isn't' builds more trust than dodging it. Contractors respect a straight answer about money.

PRICE_UPFRONT.label: What's this going to cost me?
PRICE_UPFRONT.script: Fair question — the preview costs nothing, that part's already done. Getting it finished and live runs like any of our builds, and I'll give you a real number once I know what you actually want built out. Want to see it first, then we talk numbers?
PRICE_UPFRONT.training_note: Never quote a price before they've seen the mockup and said they want it live. Redirect to 'see it first' every time.

ALREADY_HAVE_SITE.label: I already have a website
ALREADY_HAVE_SITE.script: Didn't think so when I built this — I do this for guys who don't have one yet. If I've got bad info, tell me your site and I'll take a real look instead. Otherwise, want to see what I built?
ALREADY_HAVE_SITE.training_note: Confirm/deny fast, don't get defensive. If they do have a real site, log ALREADY_HAS_SITE — that routes them back to the standard cold-call queue instead of staying here.

NOT_INTERESTED.label: Not interested
NOT_INTERESTED.script: Fair enough. It's already built and sitting there either way — want the link so it's in your pocket if you change your mind? Zero effort on your end.
NOT_INTERESTED.training_note: The ask costs them nothing, so 'not interested' rarely survives a second, lower-pressure offer of the same thing.

BUSY_NOW.label: Busy / bad time
BUSY_NOW.script: No problem — ten seconds: I built {business_name} a working homepage, already done, live right now. Want me to text you the link so you can look whenever?
BUSY_NOW.training_note: Busy is not a no. The ask is small enough to survive almost any 'not now.'

is_this_my_real_site.label: Wait, is this live? Is this my actual site now?
is_this_my_real_site.script: No — this is a private preview, not indexed, nobody can find it searching your name. It's a real working demo of what your actual site could look like. If you want it live for real — hosted, your domain, findable on Google — that's the next step.
is_this_my_real_site.training_note: Clear this up fast if asked. You never want them thinking they already have a free live site, or confused later when you ask them to pay for the real build.

send_me_something_instead.label: Just send me something / email only
send_me_something_instead.script: Done — I'll text/email the link right now. One thing though — when's good for me to follow up once you've had a look? Even a rough day works.
send_me_something_instead.training_note: Never let 'send it' be the end of the call. Get a follow-up window before you hang up — that's what turns MOCKUP_SENT into a booked next step instead of a dead link. Log FOLLOW_UP_BOOKED with the window.

not_interested_after_seeing.label: (Follow-up call) Saw it, not interested
not_interested_after_seeing.script: No worries — can I ask what didn't land? Wrong look, timing, or just not something you need right now? Helps me not waste your time again.
not_interested_after_seeing.training_note: Cheap, valuable question. The answer tells you whether to nurture (timing), drop clean (not needed), or flag a design-quality pattern if you hear it more than once across prospects.

closing.soft_close: Take a real look at it when you get a chance. If you like what you see, let's talk about getting it finished and live — no pressure either way.
closing.hard_close: Since you're into it — I can have the real version finished, hosted on your own domain, and live in about 14 days. Want me to send you the numbers?
closing.hot_close: Then let's not sit on it — I'll get you a proposal today and we can have this live inside two weeks. Sound good?
closing.training_note: Same rule as every other cockpit: never hang up without a concrete next step — a callback window, a proposal, or a booked follow-up. 'Call me if you're interested' is not a next step, it's a hope. Use hard_close/hot_close when qualify.interest_level came back strongly positive; use soft_close when they're lukewarm-but-not-a-no.

post_reveal_pitch._note: Use on the FOLLOW-UP call after they've already seen the mockup — this is where 'calling' turns into 'pitching.' This is where closing.* gets used.
post_reveal_pitch.script: Hey {first_name} — did you get a chance to look at the homepage I built for {business_name}?
post_reveal_pitch.training_note: If they liked it, go straight into closing.hard_close or closing.hot_close depending on temperature. If they haven't looked yet, get a specific time they will and log FOLLOW_UP_BOOKED. If they lost the link, resend it right now while you're on the phone and log MOCKUP_SENT again.
